claim: Prefrontal cortical influence over the mesolimbic system – including the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and the ventral tegmental area (VTA) – is implicated in various cognitive processes and behavioral malfunctions.
source: Prefrontal cortical influence over the mesolimbic system – including the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and the ventral tegmental area (VTA) – is implicated in various cognitive processes and behavioral malfunctions.
evidence: This is a general statement about the functional role of the prefrontal-mesolimbic system, supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: NAc-projecting mPFC neurons (mPFCNAc) and VTA-projecting mPFC neurons (mPFCVTA) show different laminar distribution, with mPFCNAc in layers 2/3–5a and mPFCVTA in layers 5b–6.
source: We demonstrated that NAc- (mPFCNAc) and VTA-projecting mPFC (mPFCVTA) populations show different laminar distribution (layers 2/3–5a and 5b–6, respectively)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from retrograde tracing and immunohistochemistry presented in the manuscript.

claim: Calbindin and Ntsr1 are specific to mPFCNAc neurons.
source: Specifically, calbindin and Ntsr1 are specific to mPFCNAc neurons
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular marker expression data from immunohistochemistry experiments.

claim: mPFCVTA neurons express high levels of Ctip2 and FoxP2.
source: while mPFCVTA neurons express high levels of Ctip2 and FoxP2
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular marker expression data from immunohistochemistry experiments.

claim: mPFCNAc and mPFCVTA populations are mostly separated at the cellular level.
source: indicating that these populations are mostly separated at the cellular level
evidence: This claim is supported by double retrograde tracing and viral labeling experiments showing minimal overlap.

claim: There is minimal overlap between mPFCNAc and mPFCVTA populations.
source: We directly tested this with double retrograde tracing and Canine adenovirus type 2-mediated viral labeling and found that there is indeed minimal overlap between the two populations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from double retrograde tracing and CAV2-mediated viral tracing.

claim: The projection pattern of mPFCNAc and mPFCVTA populations is different throughout the brain.
source: Furthermore, whole-brain analysis revealed that the projection pattern of these populations is also different throughout the brain.
evidence: This claim is supported by whole-brain mapping data using immunoperoxidase staining.

claim: The NAc and the VTA are innervated by two, mostly nonoverlapping mPFC populations with different laminar distribution and molecular profile.
source: Taken together, we demonstrated that the NAc and the VTA are innervated by two, mostly nonoverlapping mPFC populations with different laminar distribution and molecular profile.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by multiple experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: mPFC provides the major source of glutamatergic input to the NAc.
source: mPFC provides the major source of glutamatergic input to the NAc (Brog et al., 1993; Asher and Lodge, 2012; Li et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: mPFC provides glutamatergic input to the VTA.
source: and to the VTA (Geisler and Zahm, 2005; Mahler and Aston-Jones, 2012; Faget et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Direct mPFC innervation in the NAc has been implicated in attention regulation.
source: Direct mPFC innervation in the NAc has been implicated in various cognitive processes and malfunctions, such as attention regulation (Christakou et al., 2004)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Direct mPFC innervation in the NAc has been implicated in impulse control.
source: impulse control (Feja and Koch, 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Direct mPFC innervation in the NAc has been implicated in addiction.
source: addiction (Schmidt et al., 2005; Peters et al., 2008; Seif et al., 2013; Domingo-Rodriguez et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Direct mPFC innervation in the NAc has been implicated in depression.
source: and depression (Vialou et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: mPFC can bidirectionally modulate neuronal activity in VTA, including NAc- and mPFC-projecting dopaminergic neurons.
source: mPFC can also bidirectionally modulate neuronal activity in VTA, including NAc- and mPFC-projecting dopaminergic neurons (Gariano and Groves, 1988; Carr and Sesack, 2000; Lodge, 2011)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Stimulation of excitatory neurons in the mPFC elicits dopamine release in the NAc via the VTA.
source: Accordingly, the stimulation of excitatory neurons in the mPFC elicits dopamine release in the NAc via the VTA (Taber et al., 1995; Karreman and Moghaddam, 1996)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Optogenetic activation of mPFC input in the VTA is reinforcing.
source: and optogenetic activation of mPFC input in the VTA is reinforcing (Beier et al., 2015; Pan et al., 2021)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Intertelencephalic (IT) cells are present in layers 2–6 (L2–6) and project to ipsi- and contralateral neocortex and striatum.
source: Intertelencephalic (IT) cells are present in layers 2–6 (L2–6) and project to ipsi- and contralateral neocortex and striatum.
evidence: This is a description of a well-established classification system for cortical neurons based on existing scientific knowledge.

claim: Neurons of the pyramidal tract (PT) class are located mostly in the L5b and innervate mostly mesencephalic and diencephalic regions.
source: Neurons of the pyramidal tract (PT, also known as extratelencephalic) class are located mostly in the L5b and innervate mostly mesencephalic and diencephalic regions.
evidence: This is a description of a well-established classification system for cortical neurons based on existing scientific knowledge.

claim: The corticothalamic (CT) class is composed of neurons in the L6 that innervate the thalamus.
source: The third, corticothalamic (CT) class is composed of neurons in the L6 that innervate the thalamus.
evidence: This is a description of a well-established classification system for cortical neurons based on existing scientific knowledge.

claim: Some studies suggest that the IT-PT-CT classification might be oversimplified and not universally applicable to all cortical areas.
source: However, some studies suggest that this classification might be oversimplified and not universally applicable to all cortical areas (Groh et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A recent publication divided prefrontal cortical neurons into even more new subtypes based on their genetic identity and connectivity.
source: Indeed, a recent publication (Gao et al., 2022) divided prefrontal cortical neurons into even more new subtypes based on their genetic identity and connectivity.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: A number of publications demonstrated that NAc- and VTA-projecting neurons are mostly nonoverlapping at the cellular level.
source: For instance, a number of publications (Pinto and Sesack, 2000; Kim et al., 2017; Cruz et al., 2021) demonstrated that NAc- and VTA-projecting neurons are mostly nonoverlapping at the cellular level.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A recent study found significant overlap between NAc- and VTA-projecting populations in the anterior cingulate cortex, demonstrating that all VTA-projecting neurons simultaneously project to NAc as well.
source: However, a recent study (Gao et al., 2020) found significant overlap between these populations in the anterior cingulate cortex, a major subregion of the mPFC demonstrating that all VTA-projecting neurons simultaneously project to NAc as well.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: Retrogradely labeled NAc-projecting mPFC cells (mPFCNAc) were present throughout the mPFC.
source: Retrogradely labeled NAc-projecting mPFC cells (mPFCNAc) were present throughout the mPFC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from retrograde tracing experiments.

claim: Parvalbumin (PV) staining delineates the dorsal and ventral borders of the prelimbic (PrL) subregion of the mPFC.
source: As it was previously reported (Mátyás et al., 2014), parvalbumin (PV) staining delineates the dorsal and ventral borders of the prelimbic (PrL) subregion of the mPFC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, asterisk).
evidence: This claim is supported by both citation to a previous study and reference to a figure showing PV staining.

claim: Calbindin (Calb1) was used to define layer 2/3 (L2/3).
source: Calbindin (Calb1) was used to define layer 2/3 (L2/3) (van Brederode et al., 1991; Sun et al., 2002)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies establishing Calb1 as a marker for L2/3.

claim: Calbindin was used to define the ventral border of the infralimbic cortex (IL), where the clearly visible L2/3 diminishes.
source: and the ventral border of the infralimbic cortex (IL), where the clearly visible L2/3 diminishes
evidence: This claim describes a methodological approach used in the study based on Calb1 staining patterns.

claim: Calbindin was used to visualize the thickening of L1, a characteristic of the deep peduncular cortex (DP).
source: as well as to visualize the thickening of L1, a characteristic of the deep peduncular cortex (DP) (Akhter et al., 2014; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, number sign)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and reference to a figure showing Calb1 staining.

claim: COUP-TF-interacting protein 2 (Ctip2) was used to outline the L5b and L6.
source: COUP-TF-interacting protein 2 (Ctip2, also known as Bcl111b) was used to outline the L5b and L6 (Arlotta et al., 2005; Ueta et al., 2014; Kim et al., 2017; Figure 1—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and reference to a figure showing Ctip2 staining.

claim: Forkhead box protein P2 (FoxP2) staining identifies the L6.
source: Furthermore, forkhead box protein P2 (FoxP2) staining identifies the L6 (Ferland et al., 2003)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study establishing FoxP2 as a marker for L6.

claim: FoxP2 staining shows the gradual thinning and disappearance of a distinct L6 toward the ventralmost part of the mPFC.
source: and the gradual thinning and disappearance of a distinct L6 toward the ventralmost part of the mPFC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D, cross)
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to a figure showing FoxP2 staining patterns.

claim: Most mPFCNAc neurons were found in the medial orbital (MO; 59.99 ± 7.57%), PrL (29.31 ± 5.25%), and IL (6.40 ± 2.33%) subregions.
source: According to the obtained molecular-based mPFC map, most mPFCNAc neurons were found in the medial orbital (MO; 59.99 ± 7.57%; n = 3 animals; N = 612/1042 cells), PrL (29.31 ± 5.25%; N = 297/1042 cells), and IL (6.40 ± 2.33%; N = 59/1042 cells) subregions
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from retrograde tracing experiments.

claim: The highest number of mPFCNAc cells (N = 513/1042 cells) was found between Bregma + 2.34 and +1.99 mm.
source: with the highest number of cells (N = 513/1042 cells) between Bregma + 2.34 and +1.99 mm
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from retrograde tracing experiments.

claim: The vast majority of mPFCNAc cells were localized in the L5a (58.64 ± 16.39%) and L2/3 (29.56 ± 7.84%).
source: At the laminar level, the vast majority of mPFCNAc cells were localized in the L5a (58.64 ± 16.39%; N = 571/1042 cells) and L2/3 (29.56 ± 7.84%; N = 324/1042 cells)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from retrograde tracing experiments.

claim: About two-thirds (68.64 ± 2.62%) of mPFCNAc neurons in the L2/3 expressed Calb1.
source: Our analysis revealed that about two-thirds (68.64 ± 2.62%, n = 3 animals, NCalb1+/FG+ = 197/289 cells; Figure 1I3, L, left bar; Table 2) of mPFCNAc neurons in the L2/3 expressed Calb1
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from confocal analysis of immunohistochemistry.

claim: Only a small proportion (2.87 ± 1.15%) of mPFCNAc neurons in L5–6 expressed Calb1.
source: while only a small proportion did so in the L5–6 (2.87 ± 1.15%, NCalb1+/FG+ = 18/655 cells; Figure 1L, middle bar; Table 2)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from confocal analysis of immunohistochemistry.

claim: Approximately one-fifth of all mPFCNAc neurons expressed Calb1 (22.78 ± 1.86%).
source: Collectively, approximately one-fifth of all mPFCNAc neurons expressed Calb1 (22.78 ± 1.86%, NCalb1+/FG+ = 215/944 cells; Figure 2L, right bar; Table 2)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from confocal analysis of immunohistochemistry.

claim: Only a small proportion of superficial (i.e., L2/3–5a) mPFCNAc cells were Ctip2 positive (8.26 ± 2.6%).
source: Confocal analysis revealed that only a small proportion of superficial (i.e., L2/3–5a) cells were Ctip2 positive (8.26 ± 2.6%, n = 3 animals, NCtip2+/FG+ = 45/767 cells; Figure 1J3, M, left bar; Table 2)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from confocal analysis of immunohistochemistry.

claim: In the deeper layers (i.e., L5b–6), the majority of mPFCNAc cells expressed Ctip2 (64.1 ± 4.76%).
source: while in the deeper layers (i.e., L5b–6), although relatively few in number, the majority of cells expressed Ctip2 (64.1 ± 4.76%, NCtip2+/FG+ = 130/204 cells; Figure 1M, middle bar; Table 2)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from confocal analysis of immunohistochemistry.

claim: Approximately one-fifth of all mPFCNAc cells expressed Ctip2 (20.8 ± 12.1%).
source: Collectively, approximately one-fifth of all mPFCNAc cells expressed Ctip2 (20.8 ± 12.1%, NCtip2+/FG+ = 175/971 cells; Figure 1M, left bar; Table 2)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from confocal analysis of immunohistochemistry.

claim: Only a negligible number of mPFCNAc cells expressed FoxP2 (2.11 ± 1.84%).
source: Finally, only a negligible number of mPFCNAc cells expressed FoxP2 (2.11 ± 1.84%, n = 3 animals, NFoxP2+/FG+ = 22/862 cells, Figure 1K3, N; Table 2)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from confocal analysis of immunohistochemistry.

claim: Most mPFCVTA neurons were localized in the PrL (26.68 ± 8.63%), MO (20.57 ± 4.46%), DP (16.54 ± 0.75%), DTT (14.12 ± 1.98%), as well as in the Cg1 (9.57 ± 3.71%), IL (8.63 ± 3.25%), and Cg2 (3.88 ± 2.33%) cortices.
source: Most mPFCVTA neurons were localized in the PrL (26.68 ± 8.63%; n = 3 animals; N = 505/1878 cells), MO (20.57 ± 4.46%; N = 398/1878 cells), DP (16.54 ± 0.75%; N = 309/1878 cells), DTT (14.12 ± 1.98%; N = 259/1878 cells), as well as in the Cg1 (9.57 ± 3.71%; N = 168/1878 cells), IL (8.63 ± 3.25%; N = 175/1878 cells), and Cg2 (3.88 ± 2.33%; N = 64/1878 cells) cortices
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from retrograde tracing experiments.

claim: The highest density of mPFCVTA neurons (N = 864/1878 cells) was found between Bregma +1.98 and +1.71 mm.
source: with the highest density (N = 864/1878 cells) between Bregma +1.98 and +1.71 mm
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from retrograde tracing experiments.

claim: Most mPFCVTA cells formed two main clusters: one in the L5b (56.82 ± 6.91%) and another in the L6 (38.38 ± 2.25%).
source: Regarding their laminar distribution, we found that most of mPFCVTA cells formed two main clusters (Figure 2 D, I1–K1, I2–K2): one in the L5b (56.82 ± 6.91%; N = 1094/1878 cells) most prominently in the PrL, MO, and Cg1–2 cortices and another in the L6 (38.38 ± 2.25%; N = 713/1878 cells) of the IL, DP, and DTT
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from retrograde tracing experiments and reference to figures.

claim: Only a marginal proportion (1.31 ± 0.5%) of all mPFCVTA cells expressed Calb1.
source: Higher magnification confocal analysis revealed that only a marginal proportion (1.31 ± 0.5%, n = 3 animals, NCalb1+/FG+ = 15/1165 cells, Figure 2I3, L; Table 3) of all mPFCVTA cells expressed Calb1.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from confocal analysis of immunohistochemistry.

claim: The vast majority of mPFCVTA neurons express Ctip2 (95.07 ± 0.6%).
source: We also quantified the Ctip2expression of mPFCVTA neurons and found that the vast majority of these cells express Ctip2 (95.07 ± 0.6%, n = 3 animals, NCtip2+/FG+ = 481/506 cells; Figure 2J3, M; Table 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from confocal analysis of immunohistochemistry.

claim: This finding is in accordance with previous results showing CTIP2 gene enrichment in mPFCVTA neurons.
source: This finding is in accordance with previous results (Kim et al., 2017) showing CTIP2 gene enrichment in mPFCVTA neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Most L6 mPFCVTA cells expressed FoxP2 (78.86 ± 8.79%).
source: Finally, most L6 mPFCVTA cells expressed FoxP2 (78.86 ± 8.79%, n = 3 animals, NFoxP2+/FG+ = 761/951 cells; Figure 2K3, N, middle bar; Table 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from confocal analysis of immunohistochemistry.

claim: In the superficial layers (L2/3–L5), only a small proportion (8.69 ± 2.13%) of mPFCVTA cells were FoxP2-positive.
source: On the other hand, in the superficial layers (L2/3–L5), only a small proportion (8.69 ± 2.13%, NFoxP2+/FG+ = 77/920 cells; Table 3) of mPFCVTA cells were FoxP2-positive (Figure 2N, left bar).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from confocal analysis of immunohistochemistry.

claim: About half of all mPFCVTA neurons expressed FoxP2 (45.93 ± 17.15%).
source: In total, about half of all mPFCVTA neurons expressed FoxP2 (45.93 ± 17.15%, NFoxP2+/FG+ = 838/1871 cells; Figure 2N, right bar; Table 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from confocal analysis of immunohistochemistry.

claim: Virally labeled cell bodies in all strains were primarily found in the PrL, IL, Cg1–2, MO, and, to a lower extent, in the DP, the ventromedial M2, the dorsal part of the DTT and the medial part of the VO cortex.
source: Virally labeled cell bodies in all strains were primarily found in the PrL, IL, Cg1–2, MO, and, to a lower extent, in the DP, the ventromedial M2, the dorsal part of the DTT and the medial part of the VO cortex (Figure 3A–E)
evidence: This claim is supported by data from viral tracing experiments shown in figures.

claim: Viral expression was always analyzed after IHC enhancement of eYFP/mCherry, because this method revealed structures and fine details otherwise not detectable.
source: Note that viral expression was always analyzed after IHC enhancement of eYFP/mCherry, because this method revealed structures – mostly thin axon branches, but also some cell bodies – and fine details (e.g., dendritic spines) otherwise not detectable (see Methods) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a methodological claim supported by reference to a supplementary figure showing the comparison.

claim: Labeled cells in the Calb1-Cre animals showed similar distribution in both mPFC and M1: most of them were found in the L2/3 with scattered cells in other cortical layers.
source: Labeled cells in the Calb1-Cre animals showed similar distribution in both cortical areas: most of them were found in the L2/3 (Muñoz-Castañeda et al., 2021) with scattered cells – most likely cortical interneurons (Staiger et al., 2004) – in other cortical layers (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, F).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from viral tracing experiments and citations to previous studies.

claim: Rbp4- and Ntsr1-expressing cells showed somewhat different distribution in the mPFC compared to M1.
source: Interestingly, Rbp4- and Ntsr1-expressing cells showed somewhat different distribution in the two cortical regions (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, C, G, H).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from viral tracing experiments shown in figures.

claim: In the Rbp4-Cre strain, virally labeled cells in the mPFC were found to some extent in the L2/3 besides the well-known L5 location, while in the M1, only the L5 population was present.
source: In the Rbp4-Cre strain, virally labeled cells in the mPFC were found to some extent in the L2/3 – especially in the ventral part of the mPFC, in the IL and DP – besides the well-known L5 location. In the M1, only the L5 population was present (Callaway, 2021; Muñoz-Castañeda et al., 2021; Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, G).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from viral tracing experiments and citations to previous studies.

claim: In the Ntsr1-Cre animals, no virally labeled neurons were found in the L6 in the mPFC, only in the L5a.
source: In the Ntsr1-Cre animals, no virally labeled neurons were found in the L6 in the mPFC, only in the L5a (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from viral tracing experiments shown in a figure.

claim: In the M1 cortex, Ntsr1-expressing labeled cells were found exclusively in the L6, as it was previously reported.
source: In the M1 cortex, Ntsr1-expressing labeled cells were found exclusively in the L6, as it was previously reported (DeNardo et al., 2015; Tasic et al., 2016; Sundberg et al., 2018; Callaway, 2021; Muñoz-Castañeda et al., 2021; Figure 3—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from viral tracing experiments and citations to previous studies.

claim: Labeled cells in the FoxP2-Cre strain were most abundant in the L6 in both mPFC and M1, however, in the mPFC there were visually more virally transduced neurons in the L5 compared to M1.
source: Regarding the FoxP2-Cre strain, we found that labeled cells were most abundant in the L6 in both cortical regions examined (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D, I), however, in the mPFC we found visually more virally transduced neurons in the L5 compared to M1.
evidence: This claim is supported by data from viral tracing experiments shown in figures.

claim: In the Thy1-Cre animals, AAV transduced cells were found in all cellular layers of both the mPFC and the M1.
source: In the Thy1-Cre animals we did not observe any difference between the two cortical regions: AAV transduced cells were found in all cellular layers of the mPFC (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E) and the M1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2J).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from viral tracing experiments shown in figures.

claim: In the Calb1-Cre strain, labeled axons were found in the NAc but not in the VTA.
source: In the Calb1-Cre strain – where viral transduced cells were confined to the L2/3 – labeled axons were found in the NAc (Figure 3F) but not in the VTA (Figure 3K).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from viral tracing experiments shown in figures.

claim: In the Rbp4-Cre animals, AAV-labeled axons were found both in the NAc and VTA.
source: In the Rbp4-Cre animals (L2/3–5), AAV-labeled axons were found both in the NAc (Figure 3G) and VTA (Figure 3L)
evidence: This claim is supported by data from viral tracing experiments shown in figures.

claim: Ntsr1-Cre-expressing cells projected to the NAc with visually dense arborization but avoided the VTA.
source: Ntsr1-Cre-expressing cells – localized in the L5a (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), where most of the mPFCNAc neurons were found previously (Figure 1) – projected to the NAc with visually dense arborization (Figure 3H) but avoided the VTA (Figure 3M).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from viral tracing experiments shown in figures.

claim: In the FoxP2-Cre strain, only a small number of AAV-labeled axons was present in the NAc, while a relatively dense arborization of labeled axons was found in the VTA.
source: In the FoxP2-Cre strain (L6), only a small number of AAV-labeled axons was present in the NAc (Figure 3I), while a relatively dense arborization of labeled axons was found in the VTA (Figure 3N).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from viral tracing experiments shown in figures.

claim: In the control Thy1-Cre strain, dense axonal arborization was observed both in the NAc and VTA.
source: Finally, in the control Thy1-Cre strain we observed dense axonal arborization both in the NAc (Figure 3J) and VTA (Figure 3O).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from viral tracing experiments shown in figures.

claim: Only a small proportion of all cells contained both tracers in double retrograde tracing experiments (NAc + VTA/VTA = 6.78 ± 5.97%, NAc + VTA/NAc = 1.54 ± 1.40%, NAc + VTA/total = 1.26 ± 1.12%).
source: Our results showed that only a small proportion of all cells contained both tracers (NAc + VTA/VTA = 6.78 ± 5.97%, NAc + VTA/NAc = 1.54 ± 1.40%, NAc + VTA/total = 1.26 ± 1.12%; NNAc = 269, 2940, 2551 cells, NVTA = 111, 489, 770 cells, NVTA+NAc = 0, 55, 70 cells; n = 3 mice; Figure 4D; Table 4)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from double retrograde tracing experiments.

claim: Most double-labeled cells were found in the L5.
source: and most of them were found in the L5
evidence: This claim is supported by data from double retrograde tracing experiments.

claim: mPFCNAc neurons innervated the NAc almost tenfold stronger than the VTA (RAD(VTA/NAc) = 0.11 ± 0.06).
source: This quantitative analysis showed that mPFCNAc neurons innervated the NAc almost tenfold stronger than the VTA (RAD(VTA/NAc) = 0.11 ± 0.06; n = 3 animals; Figure 5H; Table 5; Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from axon density analysis using CAV2-Cre-mediated viral tracing.

claim: mPFCVTA cells innervated preferentially the VTA as opposed to the NAc (RAD(VTA/NAc) = 3.45 ± 0.41).
source: On the other hand, mPFCVTA cells innervated preferentially the VTA as opposed to the NAc (RAD(VTA/NAc) = 3.45 ± 0.41; n = 3 animals; Figure 5H; Table 5; Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from axon density analysis using CAV2-Cre-mediated viral tracing.

claim: mPFCRbp4 cells innervated both NAc and VTA similarly (RAD(VTA/NAc) = 0.88 ± 0.49).
source: Our analysis revealed that mPFCRbp4 cells innervated both regions similarly (RAD(VTA/NAc) = 0.88 ± 0.49; n = 3 animals; Figure 5F, H; Table 5; Figure 5—source data 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from axon density analysis using viral tracing in Rbp4-Cre mice.

claim: mPFCThy1 cells tended to innervate NAc slightly more intensively (RAD(VTA/NAc) = 0.53 ± 0.28).
source: while mPFCThy1 cells tended to innervate NAc slightly more intensively (RAD(VTA/NAc) = 0.53 ± 0.28; n = 3 animals; Figure 5G, H; Table 5; Figure 5—source data 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from axon density analysis using viral tracing in Thy1-Cre mice.

claim: mPFCNAc neurons projected intensively to the ipsi- and contralateral striatum, various cortical areas, and the amygdala.
source: Most notably, mPFCNAc neurons projected intensively to the ipsi- and contralateral striatum – including the NAc (Figure 6C, left) –, various cortical areas (Figure 6A–H, left), and the amygdala (Figure 6F, left).
evidence: This claim is supported by whole-brain projection pattern analysis data shown in figures.

claim: mPFCVTA innervation was strongest in the lateral (LS) and medial septum (MS), the hypothalamus (HT), the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST), the midline thalamic nuclei, the zona incerta (ZI) and various tectal, tegmental, and pontine regions.
source: On the other hand, mPFCVTA innervation was strongest in the lateral (LS) and medial septum (MS; Figure 6C, right), the hypothalamus (HT), the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST; Figure 6D–F, right), the midline thalamic nuclei (Figure 6E, F), the zona incerta (ZI; Figure 6F, right) and various tectal (Figure 6G, H, right), tegmental – including the VTA – (Figure 6G–I, right) and pontine regions (Figure 6G–I, right).
evidence: This claim is supported by whole-brain projection pattern analysis data shown in figures.

claim: mPFCNAc and mPFCVTA populations differ in their projection patterns not only in the NAc and VTA, but throughout the brain.
source: Taken together, our investigation revealed that mPFCNAc and mPFCVTA populations differ in their projection patterns not only in the NAc and VTA, but throughout the brain.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by whole-brain projection pattern analysis data.

claim: mPFCNAc and mPFCVTA neuron populations are mostly separated in the L2/3–5a and L5b–6, respectively, although this separation is not exclusive.
source: Taken together, our classical retrograde and cell type-specific anterograde viral tracing experiments revealed that mPFCNAc and mPFCVTA neuron populations are mostly separated in the L2/3–5a and L5b–6, respectively, although this separation is not exclusive.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by multiple experimental findings from retrograde and anterograde tracing.
